name: Fulfillment
statusNote: Full core loop built; remaining work is a final art, audio, and cockpit-UI pass tracked in a Placeholder Ledger. Built syntax-checked, pending a real play-test.
oneLiner: A deterministic, corporate-parody space wave-survival roguelite in Godot 4.7 — fly delivery runs for a satirical megacorp, survive escalating waves, draft upgrades between runs.
stack: Config as typed Godot Resource (.tres) files
HTML mockups as the approved visual spec

components.name: app
components.desc: Root state machine, save/meta progression, procedural synth SFX — owns no gameplay logic.

components.name: engine (sim)
components.desc: Deterministic fixed-60Hz step root and GameWorld, the single mutable source of truth.

components.name: engine/data
components.desc: Tunable static tables: weapons, archetypes, rarity, elements, upgrades, drafts, evolutions, hulls.

components.name: engine/systems
components.desc: Static functions run in fixed order: flight, spawn, status, enemies, hull, turrets, combat, progression.

components.name: engine/util
components.desc: Determinism primitives — the one seeded RNG, object pools, math helpers.

components.name: render
components.desc: One-way read-only rendering: hybrid batched swarm draw, cockpit HUD, radar view.

components.name: ui
components.desc: Shell screens — title, results, depot, pause, settings, draft and rack views.

components.name: docs
components.desc: DECISIONS.md manifest, ARCHITECTURE.md map with the Placeholder Ledger, HANDOFF, SPEC, CHANGELOG.

dataFlow: Keys and mouse feed an InputState snapshot.
The sim steps at a fixed 60 Hz; the seeded world RNG is the only gameplay randomness.
Systems run in strict order and mutate GameWorld, the single source of truth.
The renderer and HUD read GameWorld one-way — they never write back.
A hybrid draw batches swarm primitives and uses node scenes for the ship, bosses, and HUD.
Cosmetic event lists drain into audio and particles without touching the sim's RNG stream.
integrations: None beyond the Godot 4.7 engine — single-player, local save, no network
decisions: Strict sim-versus-render separation is a non-negotiable constraint: sim is truth, render is read-only.
One seeded RNG stream is the only gameplay randomness; cosmetics get separate RNGs.
No system is in until it's fleshed mechanically and visually and cross-checked — no orphaned mechanics ship.
A Placeholder Ledger tracks every visual stand-in; a placeholder that stops being live-wired gets deleted, not left stale.
Built in the spirit of an older wave-survival game, explicitly greenfield rather than a port.
Files follow the house split rule: review at 300 lines, split by 500.
